works.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
works.thirdPartyNotice: Independent listing. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the author, the publishers or the rights holders of Harry Potter.
works.description: The first novel in the Harry Potter series, in which an orphaned boy learns he is a wizard and starts at a school of magic. Listed as one work with its US and UK editions, which carry different titles.

editions.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
editions.note: US edition. Some catalogue records give 1998, the year of the original hardcover.
UK edition, New Children's Edition.

sources.label: University of Southern Indiana library record

works.title: Harry Potter: A History of Magic
works.thirdPartyNotice: Independent listing. Forbidden Mantra Press is not affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by the author, the publishers or the rights holders of Harry Potter.
works.description: The book of the British Library's exhibition on the history of magic, published by Bloomsbury. It surveys the real traditions of magic, alchemy and folklore alongside the Harry Potter stories.

editions.note: Paperback ISBN reported by Wikipedia only.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Harry Potter: A History of Magic

works.title: The Hobbit
works.subtitle: Or There and Back Again
works.description: Tolkien's fantasy of a reluctant hobbit drawn into a quest to reclaim a treasure guarded by a dragon. The shorter, lighter book that precedes The Lord of the Rings, and a common first step into modern fantasy.

editions.note: Listings credit Houghton Mifflin Harcourt or its Mariner Books imprint.

works.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
works.subtitle: Being the First Part of The Lord of the Rings
works.description: The first volume of The Lord of the Rings, in which the journey of the One Ring begins. Longer and darker than The Hobbit.

editions.note: Some listings credit other imprints; the Mariner/Houghton Mifflin Harcourt attribution is the most consistent.

works.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
works.description: A young mage learns the cost of power at a school of wizardry in Le Guin's archipelago of Earthsea. A cornerstone of modern fantasy, with an emphasis on balance and true names.

editions.note: Includes a new afterword by the author, per library records.
The Earthsea Cycle, Book 1.

works.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
works.description: Four children enter a snowbound land through a wardrobe in C.S. Lewis's classic of children's fantasy, the best-known book of The Chronicles of Narnia.

editions.note: Listings give different years for this ISBN, so none is shown. Illustrated by Pauline Baynes.

works.title: Good Omens
works.subtitle: The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch
works.description: A comic fantasy about an angel and a demon who try to prevent the end of the world, written by two authors who became leading voices in British fantasy.

editions.note: Publisher attribution differs between sources.

works.title: American Gods
works.description: Gaiman's novel in which old gods brought to America by immigrants clash with newer gods of media and technology. A bridge between modern fantasy and the world's mythologies.

editions.note: Other editions, including a tenth-anniversary edition, carry different ISBNs.

works.title: The Color of Magic
works.description: The first Discworld novel: a failed wizard and a tourist with a sentient luggage travel a flat world. A comic introduction to Pratchett's long-running series. Listed with its US and UK editions, which spell the title differently.

editions.note: US edition, spelled "Color".

editions.title: The Colour of Magic
editions.note: UK edition, spelled "Colour". ISBN seen on the Penguin UK page only.

works.title: Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell
works.description: An alternate-history novel in which magic returns to nineteenth-century England through two rival magicians, written in the manner of period fiction and full of footnotes.

editions.note: ISBN from a single library record.
Current Bloomsbury edition per one bookseller; 864 pages.

works.title: Circe
works.description: A retelling of Greek myth from the point of view of the witch Circe, who appears in the Odyssey. A route from classical myth into the modern novel.

works.title: The Name of the Wind
works.description: The first volume of the Kingkiller Chronicle, in which a legendary figure tells the story of his youth, including his time at a university of magic.

editions.note: Sources describe it as both mass-market and trade paperback; page counts vary.

works.title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
works.description: The first Mistborn novel: a heist against an immortal emperor, built around a magic system drawn from metals.

editions.note: Trade paperback, from library records. A mass-market edition has a different ISBN.

works.title: A Game of Thrones
works.description: The first novel of A Song of Ice and Fire, an epic of rival noble houses that is the basis of the television series Game of Thrones.

editions.note: Sources disagree on whether this is a tie-in or standard paperback and on its page count, so no year is shown.

works.title: The Once and Future King
works.description: T.H. White's retelling of the Arthurian legend, from Arthur's boyhood to the fall of Camelot, mixing humour with tragedy.

editions.note: Mass-market paperback; other Ace printings have different ISBNs.

works.title: Neverwhere
works.description: A man falls into London Below, a hidden city beneath the real one. Gaiman's urban fantasy began as a BBC television series.

editions.note: Later Morrow paperback.

works.title: The Haunting of Hill House
works.description: A classic haunted-house novel in which a paranormal investigator invites guests to stay in a notorious mansion. Known for psychological suspense.

editions.note: Revised edition.

works.title: Dracula
works.description: Stoker's 1897 vampire novel, told through letters and diaries. This Penguin Classics edition has an introduction and notes by Maurice Hindle.

editions.note: Edited by Maurice Hindle with a preface by Christopher Frayling.

works.title: Frankenstein
works.subtitle: Or, The Modern Prometheus
works.description: Mary Shelley's novel of a scientist and the being he creates, often called the first science-fiction novel. This Penguin Classics edition uses the 1831 text with introduction and notes by Maurice Hindle.

editions.note: Revised 2003 printing of the 1985 Penguin Classics edition.

works.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
works.description: A dark carnival arrives in a small Midwestern town in Bradbury's fantasy of autumn, fear and temptation.

editions.note: Library records agree on this ISBN; other S&S paperbacks have different ISBNs.

works.title: The Master and Margarita
works.description: Bulgakov's satirical novel in which the devil visits Soviet Moscow, interwoven with a retelling of the trial of Pontius Pilate. Penguin Classics Deluxe edition, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky.

editions.note: 50th-anniversary Deluxe edition with a foreword by Boris Fishman.

works.title: Interview with the Vampire
works.description: Anne Rice's first Vampire Chronicles novel, in which a vampire tells the story of his life to a reporter.

editions.note: The same ISBN appears on several Ballantine printings, so no year is shown.

works.title: The Complete Fairy Tales of the Brothers Grimm
works.subtitle: All-New Third Edition
works.description: A translation of the Grimms' collected tales by Jack Zipes, with tales omitted from the original German edition.

editions.note: All-New Third Edition; illustrated by John B. Gruelle.

works.title: Norse Mythology
works.description: Gaiman's retelling of the Norse myths, from the creation of the world to Ragnarok.

editions.note: Hardcover ISBN from one library record.

works.title: The Golden Bough
works.subtitle: A Study in Magic and Religion
works.description: Frazer's historically influential and much-criticised comparative study of magic and religion, here in the Oxford World's Classics abridgement edited by Robert Fraser.

editions.note: A new abridgement from the second and third editions.

works.title: Meditations
works.description: Marcus Aurelius's private notes on Stoic practice, in Gregory Hays's modern translation.

editions.note: One library record gives 2002.

works.title: The Republic
works.description: Plato's dialogue on justice and the ideal city, in the Penguin Classics translation by Desmond Lee with an introduction by Melissa Lane.

editions.note: Second revised edition with a new introduction by Melissa Lane.

works.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
works.subtitle: A Book for Everyone and No One
works.description: Nietzsche's philosophical work in the form of a prophet's speeches, in R. J. Hollingdale's Penguin Classics translation.

editions.note: Sources give different years (1961, 1969, 1974), so none is shown.

works.title: Man's Search for Meaning
works.description: Viktor Frankl's account of his years in Nazi concentration camps and of logotherapy, his meaning-centred approach to psychotherapy. It is a memoir and a work of psychology, not medical advice.

editions.note: Current Beacon paperback per one bookseller. An older 2006 edition (ISBN 9780807014295) is reported out of print and is not listed.

sources.label: AbeBooks listing noting the current edition

works.title: Letters from a Stoic
works.subtitle: Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium
works.description: A selection of Seneca's letters to Lucilius on Stoic practice, friendship and courage, translated by Robin Campbell.

editions.note: First published by Penguin in 1969.

works.title: The Apocalypse of Adam
works.description: A presentation of the Nag Hammadi text in which Adam passes on a revelation to his son Seth. It is part of Forbidden Mantra Press’s Nag Hammadi series. The audiobook is narrated by Emily K Patel.

editions.note: Print/Kindle edition listed on the owner homepage; ASIN not yet recovered.

sources.label: Amazon Audible listing seen in search results

works.title: Gayatri Mantra
works.subtitle: Light of Divine Intelligence
works.description: A guide to the Gayatri mantra, one of the best-known Vedic mantras, in the Forbidden Mantra Series.

editions.note: Kindle edition seen in category listing; ASIN not yet recovered.

sources.label: Amazon Audible listing seen in search results

works.title: Kebra Nagast
works.description: An edition of the medieval Ethiopian national epic recounting the Queen of Sheba, King Solomon and the lineage of Ethiopian kings. Listed June 2025 in paperback and Kindle.

sources.label: Amazon category/search listing summarised via web search

works.title: Weapons of the Gods
works.subtitle: An Overview of Astra & Shastra
works.description: An overview of the divine weapons (astras and shastras) described in Hindu epic literature. Book 1 of the Hindu Epic Series; listed June 2025 in paperback and Kindle.

sources.label: Amazon listing summarised via web search

works.title: Maha Mrityunjaya Mantra
works.description: A Forbidden Mantra Series guide to the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra, traditionally addressed to Shiva. Kindle edition, May 2025.

sources.label: Amazon listing summarised via web search

works.title: Invoke the Fierce
works.subtitle: Unlocking Strength and Protection with the Durga Mantra
works.description: A guide to the Durga mantra in the Forbidden Mantra Series. A Spanish edition is also reported.

sources.label: Amazon listing summarised via web search

works.title: Lakshmi Gayatri
works.description: A Forbidden Mantra Series guide to the Lakshmi Gayatri mantra.

sources.label: Amazon listing summarised via web search

works.title: Om Namah Shivaya
works.subtitle: A Sacred Practice Guide
works.description: A practice guide to the five-syllable Shaiva mantra Om Namah Shivaya. German and Spanish editions are reported but not yet individually identified.

sources.label: Amazon.in Kindle listing summarised via web search

works.title: Maa Kali Mantras and Instructions
works.description: Mantras and practice instructions devoted to Kali, listed as a Google Play e-book.

sources.label: Google Play Books listing seen in search results

works.title: Mo Pai Nei Kung
works.description: Listed on the owner homepage as a Forbidden Mantra Press title on internal energy and power cultivation. Edition details have not yet been confirmed; this is separate from the Beginning Mo Pai Nei Kung books by Shifu Lin, which are published by others.

editions.note: Edition details awaiting owner confirmation.

works.title: The Hidden Technology of Human Power
works.description: Listed on the owner homepage under biofield and energy systems. Edition details have not yet been confirmed.

editions.note: Edition details awaiting owner confirmation.

works.title: Forbidden Mantra
works.description: Listed on the owner homepage under mantra and transformation. It may refer to a single book or to the Forbidden Mantra Series; Amazon shows the series as 41 books. Awaiting owner confirmation.

editions.note: Awaiting owner confirmation.

works.title: The Power of Now
works.subtitle: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment
works.description: A short, direct introduction to present-moment awareness. Tolle argues that much suffering comes from identification with the thinking mind, and offers simple attention exercises rather than doctrine. A common first book for readers new to contemplative ideas.

editions.note: Trade paperback with new preface; page counts differ between listings so none is shown.

sources.label: eBay UK listing (ISBN, title, publisher, year)

claims.text: Seller claim: over 16 million copies sold; New York Times bestseller

works.title: The Untethered Soul
works.subtitle: The Journey Beyond Yourself
works.description: A reflective guide to observing the inner narrator and releasing habitual emotional patterns. Singer uses plain, secular-leaning language and a progression of short chapters that suit daily reading.

works.title: When Things Fall Apart
works.subtitle: Heart Advice for Difficult Times
works.description: Talks by a Tibetan Buddhist nun on staying present with pain, uncertainty and loss. The advice is drawn from the Shambhala/Vajrayana tradition but written for general readers, including those with no Buddhist background.

editions.note: 20th-anniversary edition with a new afterword.
Original edition. ISBN reported by Bookshare only; not corroborated by a second source.

sources.label: Penguin Random House Shambhala page / Parnassus listing

works.title: When the Body Says No
works.subtitle: Exploring the Stress-Disease Connection
works.description: A physician’s argument that chronic suppression of emotion and long-term stress are linked to illness. It is a clinical-psychological work built on case histories, and it is not a substitute for medical treatment.

editions.note: Earlier edition under a different subtitle, per library record.

works.title: Buckland’s Complete Book of Witchcraft
works.description: A self-study course in modern Wicca, laid out as a series of lessons. Buckland was an early figure in bringing Gardnerian Wicca to the United States, and the book reflects that initiatory-religion perspective rather than historical witchcraft.

editions.note: Second edition, revised and expanded; Practical Magick series.

works.title: Wicca
works.subtitle: A Guide for the Solitary Practitioner
works.description: An introduction to Wicca as a nature-centred religion honouring a Goddess and God, written for people practising alone rather than in a coven. It includes ritual outlines and a model Book of Shadows.

editions.note: Llewellyn’s Practical Magick series. A revised 2004 edition is listed by some libraries.

works.title: Encyclopedia of 5,000 Spells
works.subtitle: The Ultimate Reference Book for the Magical Arts
works.description: A very large alphabetical reference of spells, charms and folk-magic traditions drawn from many cultures. It is a compendium for browsing, not a single-tradition system.

editions.note: Kindle edition ISBN per Goodreads; ISBN-10 not applicable, so no ASIN-derived link.

works.title: Seventy-Eight Degrees of Wisdom
works.subtitle: A Tarot Journey to Self-Awareness
works.description: A card-by-card study of the Rider–Waite–Smith tarot that treats the deck as a language of symbols for reflection. It has remained in print since 1980 and is widely used as a foundation text for serious tarot readers.

editions.note: New edition with a new preface.
40th-anniversary edition per Kingston Frontenac Public Library record.

works.title: The Gnostic Gospels
works.description: A scholarly but readable study of the Nag Hammadi texts and what they reveal about the diversity of early Christianity. Pagels examines how the texts differ from the writings that became orthodox and why those differences mattered.

editions.note: First published by Random House in 1979.

sources.label: Bookshop.org listing (title page only; affiliate link not used)

claims.text: Won the National Book Award and the National Book Critics Circle Award

works.title: Taoist Secrets of Love
works.subtitle: Cultivating Male Sexual Energy
works.description: An early English presentation of Healing Tao practices for sexual-energy cultivation, including the Microcosmic Orbit. It is a modern teaching system adapted from Taoist internal-alchemy ideas, and its health claims are the authors’ own.

works.title: Healing Mantras
works.subtitle: Using Sound Affirmations for Personal Power, Creativity, and Healing
works.description: A practical introduction to Sanskrit mantras for specific intentions, with transliteration and instructions for use. It presents mantra practice in a form accessible to newcomers; readers interested in traditional lineage guidance should consult a teacher.
